title: Breast cyst aspiration
also: fluid removal from a breast cyst
what: Using a thin needle and ultrasound guidance, the doctor draws fluid out of a cyst in the breast. The cyst usually shrinks.
why: If the cyst is painful, large, or looks unusual, as decided by your doctor.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; a test of the fluid, if done, takes a few days
tell_doctor: Allergy to antiseptics or local numbing

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: On the day, do not put cream or deodorant on your breast.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own.

steps: You undress to the waist and lie down
The doctor finds the cyst on ultrasound
The skin is cleaned and sometimes numbed
A thin needle is put into the cyst and the fluid is drawn out
The ultrasound confirms the cyst has shrunk
The puncture site is pressed and a plaster is put on
feel: A prick, like a blood draw
Often the cyst pain goes away right after
after: You can put a cold pack on for 10 to 15 minutes
A small bruise may appear and goes away on its own
Follow-up ultrasound after the time your doctor says
red_flags: Your breast becomes very swollen, red, and hot

faq.a: Sometimes yes. It can then be drained again if your doctor thinks it is needed.
A simple cyst is usually not dangerous. The doctor will assess it on ultrasound and decide what comes next.

reminders.text: Breast cyst aspiration tomorrow. No cream or deodorant in the morning, and bring previous ultrasounds.
